properties.content: Question: gastro infection symptoms Answer: Gastrointestinal infection symptoms often include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain or cramping. Fever, dehydration, and general weakness can also occur. Symptoms typically develop within a few hours to a couple of days after exposure and can last from a few days to a week. Common Symptoms:: - Diarrhea: Frequent, loose, and watery stools. - Nausea and Vomiting: Can range from mild to severe. - Abdominal Pain/Cramps: May be mild to severe and localized to the stomach area. - Fever: Can be present in some cases. - Dehydration: Thirst, dry mouth, and decreased urination are signs. Other Possible Symptoms:: loss of appetite, headaches, body aches, and fatigue. When to Seek Medical Advice:: - If symptoms are severe or persistent (e.g., severe dehydration, bloody stools, persistent vomiting). - If you have a fever over 100.4°F (38°C). - If you are unable to keep down fluids. - If you have signs of dehydration, such as decreased urination, dry mouth, or dizziness. - If you have a serious underlying condition and have diarrhea and vomiting.

Question: gastro infection symptoms

Answer: Gastrointestinal infection symptoms often include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain or cramping. Fever, dehydration, and general weakness can also occur. Symptoms typically develop within a few hours to a couple of days after exposure and can last from a few days to a week.
Common Symptoms::
- Diarrhea: Frequent, loose, and watery stools.
- Nausea and Vomiting: Can range from mild to severe.
- Abdominal Pain/Cramps: May be mild to severe and localized to the stomach area.
- Fever: Can be present in some cases.
- Dehydration: Thirst, dry mouth, and decreased urination are signs.
Other Possible Symptoms::
loss of appetite, headaches, body aches, and fatigue.
When to Seek Medical Advice::
- If symptoms are severe or persistent (e.g., severe dehydration, bloody stools, persistent vomiting).
- If you have a fever over 100.4°F (38°C).
- If you are unable to keep down fluids.
- If you have signs of dehydration, such as decreased urination, dry mouth, or dizziness.
- If you have a serious underlying condition and have diarrhea and vomiting.
